It reports that state gratitude and state loneliness were negatively associated. The findings indicate that men generally reported higher loneliness than women, but this gender difference was moderated by age and gratitude level, being significant in young adults who were more grateful and older adults who were less grateful. The section references Fig. 1 for effect sizes and discusses conflicting evidence on gender differences in loneliness, suggesting men may be more reactive to losses than women due to differing social support networks.
